description.html: The ship wheel brings the story of a sunken ship into your aquarium. A dark brown wheel with a pronounced wood grain stands on a post, with two barrels in front of it: one upright and filled with pebbles and shells, the other tipped on its side with the opening facing forward. The post and base are painted in green tones, as if algae and moss had covered them over time.

Small fish and shrimp can swim into the tipped-over barrel and hide, and fish like to swim between the spokes of the wheel. The decoration suits small and medium aquariums, where it can be the main feature; in larger aquariums it looks best grouped with other nautical decorations, such as an anchor or a shipwreck.

Before putting it in the aquarium, rinse the decoration with lukewarm water, without soap or chemicals. Place the base on a flat part of the bottom and press it lightly into the gravel or sand so the wheel stands steadily. When algae appears on the surface, clean it with a soft brush; avoid sharp objects that could scratch the paint.
